description: Expected theme groupings for the synthetic gold ledger. Entries i01 and i02 share the same coaching point (bass onset) and should be in one theme. All other entries are distinct. When invert_distinct_default is true the scorer treats every pair as a distinct constraint except those in known_merge_pairs, so adding a new session entry automatically participates in every constraint without requiring manual enumeration.

known_merge_pairs.reason: Both address the bass onset: i01 is the problem (scoop), i02 is the exercise to fix it. Same singer, same moment, same technique.

_known_distinct_pairs_documentation: Superseded by invert_distinct_default. Listed here for readability only — the scorer ignores this field when invert_distinct_default is true and generates the full 54-pair matrix from all_entry_ids minus known_merge_pairs.

known_distinct_pairs.reason: Lead diphthong vs tenor release — different singers, different techniques.
Pickup breath (coordination exercise) vs tag tempo (avoid acceleration) — different techniques even though both are whole-quartet.
Measure repetition (practice drill) vs starting pitch owner (lead responsibility) — completely different coaching points.

Same general area (vocal technique) but different coaching points at different times: i02 is a bass onset exercise (specific drill for one singer), i11 is a resonance instruction for the whole quartet. Canonical over-merge case: similar subject area, distinct corrections.

i05 is a dynamic correction for baritone on a specific note (soften the third), i06 is a whole-quartet rehearsal technique (hum the phrase). Different targets, different techniques, different moments.

_coverage_notes: Full distinct-pair matrix: C(11,2)=55 pairs minus 1 permitted merge (i01,i02) = 54 active distinct constraints. No manually enumerated gaps remain. The gold-predicted-summary passes (10 themes: [i01,i02] merged, all others singleton). Irreducible gap: this fixture cannot test pairs of entries that do not appear in this 11-entry session; a model that over-merges on novel session content will not be caught here.
